messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing a sawtooth pattern of NVMe latency on gnode-pool during the nightly janitor scrub window, GPU launches stalled for ~30-90s spikes.

devon: Can you paste the dashboard link and any iostat/top logs? Trying to correlate with provisioning traces.

maya: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/storage/trace/3456 — traces attached. Pattern lines up with ephemeral-cleaner runs on the same hosts. Queue depth jumps when scrub starts. Sample iostat snapshot collected during spike:
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device    r/s    w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await
nvme0n1  1.2k   80    256k    1k     60.3
```

anita: @maya can we reduce janitor concurrency to 1 for affected pools tonight? That should smooth the sawtooth spikes and let GPUs provision.

maya: Done. I've queued a rollout for `janitor.concurrency=1` scoped to pool=scratch-eu-west2 on canary hosts. Monitoring now.

liam: Heads-up: reducing concurrency increases scrub backlog. Any rough numbers on impact to GPU provisioning SLO / cost?

maya: Quick calc: provisioning failures up ~2% during spikes, median launch +45s. If this persists, idle GPU minutes on preemptible fleet could add ~ $2.1k/month.

devon: Short-term mitigations we can try tonight: set `blkio.weight` for janitor pods to 50 and run scrub with `ionice -c3` to drop IO priority. Also stagger cron offsets across nodes.

maya: Applying `ionice -c3` on canary scrub process now, and adding blkio weight. Also added cron offsets to stagger starts by +/- 10m.

janitor-bot: rollout started for config `janitor.concurrency=1` on 4 hosts — status: in_progress

anita: If ionice/blkio doesn't hit the tail latency, we should consider changing the scrub read pattern to batch fewer random reads per second or add host-level `nvme-qos` throttles.

devon: Another possibility: tag a small set of "scrub-soak" nodes (scratch-drain=false) to divert heavy scrubs off gpu-provision nodes. That reduces contention without dropping overall scrub throughput.

liam: Agreed. Proposed immediate plan for tonight: 1) canary concurrency=1, 2) ionice + blkio on scrub, 3) stagger windows, 4) tag spare nodes to soak scrubs.

maya: I'll run the canary and collect latency + provisioning traces. If we stabilize I'll roll the change wider in the morning.

anita: Volunteers to watch alerts 23:00–02:00 UTC? I'll take 23:00–00:30 UTC.

devon: I'm on pager 23:30–01:30 UTC.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll escalate to an incident if provisioning_errors > 5% sustained for 10 minutes.

maya: Thanks all. If this works, next steps: implement automatic dynamic throttling for janitor when host nvme_saturation > 70% and open an RFC to change default scrub scheduling to zone-aware windows. I'll post a short follow-up with traces and timeline. :thumbsup:
